findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
findings.body: The new cleanup paths unconditionally emit Error logs before and after every batch, including when no IDs are found and no error occurred. Orphaned-tag cleanup therefore emits errors even on an idle, healthy instance. This creates false error alerts and floods production error logs; use debug-level logging for successful work and reserve Error for actual failures.

findings.title: SQLite ID-list construction is quadratic in batch size
findings.body: Each iteration formats and copies the entire accumulated ID string. For large configured SQLite batches (including the 32767 batch size introduced in the tests), constructing one DELETE allocates and copies gigabytes cumulatively rather than work proportional to the number of IDs. This can cause substantial GC pressure and delay cleanup. Build the list with a strings.Builder or append into a byte buffer instead.

findings.title: Restore the existing interval for unrelated cleanup jobs
findings.body: Changing this ticker from ten minutes to one minute runs every cleanup job ten times as frequently, not just annotation cleanup. This includes dashboard-version deletion, snapshot cleanup, temporary-file scans, and query-history retention queries. The deadlock fix does not require this scheduling change, and it adds recurring filesystem and database load across all installations. Keep the existing interval or explicitly isolate and justify an annotation-specific scheduling change.
